clue.text: How to make MD share with another

definitions.meaning: in Roman numerals M is 1000 and D is 500, so cutting M into two equal parts turns it into D
to split something into two equal portions with a second person

explanation.surface: Instructions on how a doctor (an MD) should share something with a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: MD looks like a doctor, but it is read as two Roman numerals: M (1000) cut in two gives D (500).
explanation.definitionFit: Dividing into two equal parts is both what turns 1000 into 500 and what splitting with a partner means.

clue.text: Man on call, an undistinguished sounding character?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: homo is Latin for man, as in Homo sapiens
to call someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A man taking a phone call is described as a dull-sounding fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undistinguished sounding' means not told apart by its sound: a word pronounced like a different word.
explanation.definitionFit: A word pronounced exactly like a different word cannot be told apart by ear, a character whose sound is indistinguishable.

clue.text: Vessel foundering in River Nile

indicators.note: a ship foundering breaks up and sinks, so the letters of the river's name are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A boat sinking in the River Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foundering' rearranges NILE as LINE; the R for River goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a large passenger ship, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Gulf Arab in prison rising, self-centred type

indicators.note: in places the Gulf Arab within the prison word
in a down clue rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement, a prison
an Omani is a native of Oman, a Gulf state

explanation.surface: An Arab from the Gulf, rising in prison, is a selfish sort.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads the prison word upwards, giving EGAC; Oman is one of the Arab states on the Gulf, and 'in' sets its native inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A person obsessed with themselves, wholly self-absorbed, is a self-centred type.

clue.text: Shot played in traditional fashion

parts.note: square means old-fashioned or conventional
the cut of a garment is its style or fashion

explanation.surface: A stroke performed in the old-fashioned manner.
explanation.walkthrough: A square cut is a cricket stroke hitting the ball square of the wicket on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket stroke sending the ball out square on the off side is a shot a batsman plays.

clue.text: Port of poet on the drink

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another stands above it, coming first

parts.note: Shakespeare was called the Sweet Swan of Avon, so a poet can be a swan
the drink is slang for the sea

explanation.surface: The harbour town of a poet who is out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Jonson called Shakespeare the 'Sweet Swan of Avon'. The Welsh port was also the home town of the poet Dylan Thomas, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh coastal city with docks on the Bristol Channel is a port.

clue.text: It may be why, we hear, one's not famous

definitions.text: It may be why, we hear
definitions.meaning: the letter Y, which sounds like why, stands for an unsolved quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Perhaps the reason, people say, someone is not a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'why' is the letter Y as spoken; in algebra x and y are the quantities to be found. 'one's' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra the letters x and y stand for quantities still to be found; and an obscure person lacks any fame.

clue.text: Get out of bed one of several English flowers

definitions.meaning: to wake up and get up from sleep
a flower is something that flows, a river; several English rivers share the name Ouse, and R for river stands before the name

explanation.surface: Rise early to see one of England's many blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' wants to be blooms; it means rivers. There are Ouse rivers in Yorkshire, Sussex and East Anglia, and a map writes one as R. plus its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Waking and getting up is the first sense; a river named Ouse, labelled with R for river, is the second.

clue.text: For journalist writing Times leader, space in the paper, is needed first

indicators.note: says the column and the 'is' must come before the Times leader in the answer

parts.note: a column is a vertical section of newspaper space

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Times

explanation.surface: A journalist writing a Times editorial needs to secure newspaper space first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like a newspaper editorial but only takes the first letter of Times. 'needed first' puts COLUMN and IS ahead of that T; 'For' and 'writing' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer with a regular signed feature in a newspaper is a kind of journalist.

clue.text: Strong man said to increase pressure

indicators.note: said signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken, giving a word of matching sound

parts.note: to tighten something is to increase the pressure or tension on it

explanation.surface: A muscleman is reported to be applying more pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the giant gods who preceded the Olympians were of enormous strength, so a powerful man takes their name.

clue.text: To get woollen cloth, pawn old boat for explorer

parts.note: mungo is cheap cloth made from recycled woollen rags
P is the chess notation for a pawn
Noah's ark is the most famous old boat

explanation.surface: Pawning an old boat to raise money for some woollen material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pawn' looks like a verb (to hock) but is the chess piece. Mungo Park (1771-1806) was a Scottish explorer of the River Niger. 'To get' and 'for' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish surgeon who traced the Niger in West Africa is a famous explorer.

clue.text: A place for the rest of the French in dark

parts.note: un is the French for a, the French language being signalled by 'of the French'

parts.words: place for the rest of the French
parts.note: lit is the French word for bed, a place for rest

explanation.surface: A French spot for a nap, in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the French' tells you to translate both 'A' and 'place for the rest' into French: un lit, a bed. 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A room with no lamp switched on is in darkness, hence dark.

clue.text: Daughter finally caught by parents in Italian city

indicators.note: caught by means held inside the parents' letters

parts.note: pa and ma are the two parents

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word Daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter is at last caught by her parents in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parents' gives both parents as nursery names, father then mother, and 'caught by' holds the daughter's last letter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern Italian home of the famous ham and cheese is a city in Italy.

clue.text: Representative pushes mother into partnership

indicators.note: into puts the pushes and mother words inside the partnership letters

parts.note: in bridge North and South play as partners, abbreviated N and S
pokes means prods or pushes
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: An agent shoves his mother into a business partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partnership' looks like a business; it is the bridge pair North-South, its S and N wrapped around the other two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who speaks on behalf of a group or firm is its representative.

clue.text: Instrument's zero reading in a vehicle inside

indicators.note: inside places the vehicle within the zero and 'in a' sequence

parts.note: a dial reading zero shows 0, the letter O
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An instrument shows nought while sitting inside a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts CAR between the O and the IN A: O-CAR-IN A. The 's of 'Instrument's' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Club for female in mostly amateur organization

indicators.note: in puts the female inside the rearranged amateur letters
organization means arranging, so the letters are put into a new order
mostly means the word amateur loses its final letter

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A club for women within a largely amateur body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts amateur to AMATEU, 'organization' rearranges it as ATAEUM, and 'in' puts HEN inside: AT-HEN-AEUM. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A London gentlemen's club in Pall Mall bears this name, so it is a club.

clue.text: A 9, probably, should remove: you from hazard

definitions.text: A 9, probably, should remove: you from hazard

parts.words: A 9, probably, should remove: you from hazard
parts.note: an old lofted golf club, close to a modern nine-iron, is the one used to lift a ball out of a bunker, a golf hazard

explanation.surface: A nine-iron ought to get you out of trouble on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: The page has no colon after 'remove'. The old name for this steeply lofted iron matches roughly a modern 9-iron, and bunkers are golf's hazards.
explanation.definitionFit: An old lofted golf iron, roughly a modern nine-iron, is the club for chipping a ball out of sand traps.

clue.text: Brave infantry given jet cover

indicators.note: in a down clue the covering piece sits on top, so it comes first

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
foot soldiers are the infantry, called the foot

explanation.surface: Courageous foot soldiers are given air cover by jet planes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective but is a noun: a Native American warrior, and the Blackfoot are a Plains people. 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American warrior, called a brave, could belong to this northern Plains nation.

clue.text: Paving to replace broken set?

indicators.note: to replace is to place again, so the letters of broken set are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Paving stones are needed to replace a broken set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' looks like the anagram signal for 'set', but it is part of the fodder; 'replace' does the rearranging. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone edging the pavement forms part of the paving along a street.

clue.text: Learner I teach in way that's professionally correct

indicators.note: in a way here means in a different way, so the letters of I teach are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A trainee says I teach in a manner that meets professional standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in way' rearranges I TEACH as ETHICA, and the Learner's L goes at the end, though the clue names it first. 'that's' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour meeting a profession's moral code is right by that code's standards.

clue.text: For example, kid's ball

definitions.meaning: kid is soft skin from a young goat, one example of tanned hide
in cricket slang the ball is called by the name of its hide cover

explanation.surface: Say, a child's ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child; it is goatskin. A cricket ball is stitched from hide, hence its nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidskin is one type of tanned hide, and a cricket ball, being covered in hide, takes the same name.

clue.text: Destroy second victim of mercury poisoning?

parts.note: felt hat makers used mercury compounds and suffered poisoning, hence 'mad as a hatter'

explanation.surface: Wreck a second person poisoned by mercury.
explanation.walkthrough: Felt-hat makers absorbed mercury in their work, which caused tremors and madness; the question mark flags this example.
explanation.definitionFit: To smash something into fragments is to destroy it.

clue.text: Doubtful American thus protected inside

definitions.note: read as an American who doubts, a noun phrase, with the American spelling

indicators.note: inside places the protected word within the word for thus

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used in quotations
kept means preserved or protected

explanation.surface: A suspicious American is therefore safeguarded indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The K spelling is American; British usage writes C. 'Doubtful' works as 'a doubter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person inclined to question claims is a doubter, and this spelling with K is the US form.

clue.text: Trap set round a watering-hole

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals

indicators.note: round means the set word goes around the a

parts.note: to set something down is to place it

explanation.surface: A snare is laid around a drinking pool for animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watering-hole' looks like a pool for animals but is slang for a bar; a gin palace was a gaudy Victorian pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A showy Victorian pub selling spirits is a drinking establishment, slangily a watering-hole.

clue.text: Talks a lot of hot air, say

definitions.meaning: hot air is an example of vapours such as oxygen and nitrogen

explanation.surface: Someone talks a great deal of empty nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot air' looks like the idiom for empty talk, but here it is literally warm vapour. 'of' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To chatter on at length is to blather, and warm atmosphere consists of vapours like nitrogen.

clue.text: Joint withdrawal from bank legally made

indicators.note: a withdrawal from a bank takes something out, here letters taken out of bank legally

explanation.surface: Two account holders lawfully take money out of their shared bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a shared account; it is a body part. 'made' is a link closing the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinge between foot and leg is a joint of the body.

clue.text: So noble almost returned in glory

indicators.note: returned means the whole sequence is turned back to front
almost means the noble's title loses its final letter

parts.note: a duke is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A nobleman, nearly back home, basking in glory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts DUKE to DUK; 'returned' reverses SO + DUK as one run. 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise and renown earned by achievement amount to glory.

clue.text: Halved before being quartered?

definitions.meaning: in golf a halved hole or match is one finished level, with neither side winning
the traitor's sentence was to be hanged, disembowelled and then cut into four

explanation.surface: Cut in two before being cut into four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halved' looks like cutting in two, but it is a level result in golf. The old English penalty for treason ran hanged, drawn and quartered.
explanation.definitionFit: A tied game is a level result, and in the old traitor's punishment disembowelling came just before quartering.

clue.text: Declare head of state, then crown

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word state

parts.note: a crown is the top or summit, a peak

explanation.surface: Proclaim the head of state and then crown them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' and 'crown' suggest a coronation; 'head of' takes only S. 'then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something is to state or utter it in words.

clue.text: Spicy vegetable one would prefer to avoid

parts.note: hot means spicy, as with chilli
a potato is a root vegetable

explanation.surface: A peppery vegetable dish people would rather skip.
explanation.definitionFit: A controversial issue nobody wants to handle is something people would rather sidestep.

clue.text: Like bid unchanged on reflection?

parts.note: the lower-case letters of bid look the same in a mirror, the b and d swapping places around the central i

explanation.surface: Describing an auction offer that stays the same after reconsideration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' looks like second thoughts about a bid; it is a mirror image of the written word.
explanation.definitionFit: Having mirror-image halves either side of a centre line describes the written word bid, whose b and d reflect each other.

clue.text: At least score by end of game is tight

parts.note: tens, as in 'tens of people', means at least two tens, so at least a score of twenty

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word game

explanation.surface: Having a score of at least twenty by the close of a match makes things nervy.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, and 'tens' (as in 'tens of thousands') implies at least two of them. 'by' joins the pieces; 'is' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope drawn taut and stretched is tight.
